```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import wade
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent / "tools"))
import tcga_examples as TC
from notebook_support import output_dir, markdown_table, export_table
OUT = output_dir("prostate")
cohort = TC.load_cohort("prostate", OUT)
PANEL = TC.PROSTATE_PANEL
SHOW = ["gene","status","bulk_shift","upper_tail","lower_tail","padj"]
def table(frame,name):
    markdown_table(frame,OUT,name)
```

## Prespecified design

Use full **gene counts** and one library per patient and sample class. The
primary unpaired comparison retains eligible normal-adjacent samples and
excludes their paired tumours, leaving independent patients. Technical and
population exclusions are fixed before gene testing; cases are not removed
because they weaken a signal. Exact retained IDs and exclusions are exported. Every gene, normalization
reference and stopping record is retained. All results and figures require
user approval.

RLE is fitted on the full measured gene universe after primary sample selection.
The prespecified example test mask requires at least 10 counts in five pooled
samples and pooled mean CPM at least 0.1, using the eligible input cohort.
This is an example recipe, not a universal threshold. Test filtering reuses
the fitted factors. Expression is `log2(count / size_factor + 1)`; no noise is
added. Repeated observations, depth and tissue mixture remain relevant to
interpretation. The upstream count processing/reference record remains a
release documentation requirement.

```{python}
#| label: accounting
#| output: asis
primary_meta = cohort.meta[cohort.independent.tolist()]
table(primary_meta.group_by("group").len(),"primary-accounting")
```

## Whole-transcriptome distribution test

Use exact empirical W1 and the production stopping rule, cap 499,999, seed 1.
BH corrects the complete retained family once. Display markers were fixed in
advance; their inclusion does not imply significance. A q-value tests the gene's
whole distribution, not its bulk sign or a particular tail.

```{python}
#| label: primary
#| output: false
res = TC.run(cohort,cohort.independent,OUT,"primary")
annotation_values = TC.annotation_expression(cohort,res,PANEL)
export_table(annotation_values,OUT,"panel-expression-annotations")
```

```{python}
#| label: transcriptome-calls
#| output: asis
calls=int(np.sum(res.padj <= .05))
table(pl.DataFrame({"Tested genes":[int(res.tested.sum())],"Distribution calls":[calls],
                    "Called fraction":[calls/res.tested.sum()]}),"transcriptome-calls")
```

These broad call sets require review of the normalization reference, tissue
mixture and technical effects. Marker recovery does not establish their
real-data false discovery proportion.

## Fusion-associated expression

The [TCGA prostate study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2015.10.025) supplies
fusion and expression-high annotations via the frozen cBioPortal study records.
The exact source responses and checksums accompany the analysis. Fusion,
expression-high, negative and unknown remain distinct. RNA-based ascertainment
is not automatically independent of expression, and expression-high status is
not a confirmed fusion.

```{python}
#| label: fusion-coverage
#| output: asis
rows=[]
for gene in ["ERG","ETV1","ETV4","FLI1"]:
    m=primary_meta.filter(pl.col("group")=="tumor")
    for category in ["fusion","high","none",None]:
        selected=m.filter(pl.col(gene+"_STATUS").is_null() if category is None else pl.col(gene+"_STATUS")==category)
        rows.append(dict(gene=gene,annotation=category or "unknown",patients=selected.height))
table(pl.DataFrame(rows),"fusion-coverage")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-etv1
#| fig-cap: "ETV1 in the independent-patient primary cohort. An upper-tail description can coexist with a negative bulk shift."
res.plot_gene("ETV1")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-etv4
#| fig-cap: "ETV4 in the same primary cohort. The reported q-value is the actual current-method result, whether or not the marker is called."
res.plot_gene("ETV4")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-erg
#| fig-cap: "ERG provides a more prevalent fusion-associated expression example. No per-sample fusion membership is inferred by WADE."
res.plot_gene("ERG")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-fusion-expression
#| fig-cap: "ETV1 and ETV4 in the independent primary cohort, colored by supplied fusion annotations. Unknown and non-fusion tumours remain visible."
m=primary_meta
x=res.expression[res.gene_index("ETV1")]
y=res.expression[res.gene_index("ETV4")]
tumour=m["group"].to_numpy()=="tumor"
a=(m["ETV1_STATUS"]=="fusion").fill_null(False).to_numpy() & tumour
b=(m["ETV4_STATUS"]=="fusion").fill_null(False).to_numpy() & tumour
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6,4),layout="constrained")
for label,mask,color,marker in [("Other/unknown tumours",tumour & ~a & ~b,"#a0aab3","o"),
    ("ETV1 fusion",a,"#2675ac","o"),("ETV4 fusion",b,"#be4960","o"),
    ("Normal-adjacent",~tumour,"#d99143","s")]:
    ax.scatter(x[mask],y[mask],s=24,alpha=.75,color=color,marker=marker,label=label)
ax.set(xlabel="ETV1: log₂(count / size factor + 1)",ylabel="ETV4: log₂(count / size factor + 1)")
ax.legend(fontsize=9)
fig
```

The plot is an annotation association, not a ground-truth FDR assessment.
No inferred driver width or sample-level significance is reported. In particular,
few normal samples can limit a recurrent-tail test even when the highest tumour
values are extreme. This limitation motivates the later rarity work, but is
not repaired by assigning another q-value to the same descriptive tail.
